claude.notes: Prompts arrive on stdin rather than as an argument. Judge prompts carry the rubric plus every response for a case and can run past 30k characters, which exceeds the Windows command-line limit; stdin has no such cap. --setting-sources '' isolates the call from the operator's own plugins, hooks, memory, and output styles. Without it, a user-level always-on flag (~/.claude/.tldr-always) would inject the tldr ruleset into the BASELINE condition and the eval would measure the skill against itself. --model is pinned deliberately: isolation also drops the operator's saved model setting, so without a pin the eval silently runs whatever the CLI happens to default to, varying between operators and over time, and per-token cost varies with it. Record the pinned model with any published numbers.

claude-opus.notes: Same runner against the stronger model. Roughly five times the cost of the sonnet runner for the same case set. Worth it for a headline published number; the sonnet runner is the sensible default for iterating on the skill, and is closer to what most users actually run.

claude-haiku.notes: Cheap runner for smoke-testing the harness end to end before committing to a full run. Do not publish numbers from this one as a headline result: a style skill behaves differently on a small model, and the comparison is only meaningful against the model you actually claim it for.

codex.notes: --ignore-user-config --ephemeral is the Codex equivalent of the isolation above. Keep it.

gemini.notes: Gemini CLI loads GEMINI.md from the working directory. Run this harness from a directory that does not contain one, or the context file leaks into every condition. Note that this repository ships a GEMINI.md at its root.
